reservoir_ep09_001.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_001.text: On Day One Thousand One Hundred, Jing's accepted blank settled before Yue's first changed-temperature sample. The room began at its registered cool condition, ordinary enough that Yue could hear somebody outside complaining about tea. Her recovered usable inventory after sleep and morning movement measured seventy and three quarters before sampling. The quarter-unit sample left seventy and a half. It was already below the local seventy-two requirement. Mei repeated that the bounded assessment could still examine actual temperature response; it would not become a qualifying pass because everyone had prepared the room.

reservoir_ep09_002.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_002.text: The initial compatible portion measured ninety-one and three quarters percent. Yue could see its slight improvement over the earlier baseline and the remaining gap below ninety-two. Deng did not smile at her across the room, and she was grateful. A reassuring expression might have tempted her to imagine he knew more than the comparison showed. He stood beside the ordinary stop marker. Jing read the actual room temperature aloud. Yue repeated the planned low-load task and its familiar application ceiling before beginning.

reservoir_ep09_003.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_003.text: The familiar four-breath task consumed half a unit from the measured usable reserve and produced its already rated quarter-unit useful application. No ordinary breath carried more than an eighth. The task and full grounded release left seventy usable before the registered warm condition was introduced. Ordinary attendants adjusted the room within its stated mild range. They used no furnace blast or sudden freezing exposure. Yue felt her collar grow warmer and noticed an urge to shorten the pause. She named that urge when Mei asked for her present condition.

reservoir_exam_failure.speaker: narrator
reservoir_exam_failure.text: Under the warmer comparison, the reservoir's uneven response increased. Jing's trace showed usable drift instead of the balanced retention Yue had hoped to observe. Yue tried to preserve the old pause, but her attention narrowed toward the edge of the sleeve. Mei gave the agreed stop before another sequence began. Yue released fully. The actually usable inventory settled at sixty-eight and three quarters, another one and a quarter lost to the observed drift. Its compared compatible portion had fallen to eighty-nine and three quarters percent. The first changed-temperature assessment had failed.

reservoir_ep09_005.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_005.text: Yue remained seated while Jing completed the stopped record. Seventy and three quarters at the start had become seventy and a half after sampling, seventy after the actual task, then sixty-eight and three quarters after the changed-condition drift. Neither sample nor task nor loss returned because the trial had failed. Mei marked the temperature response as unstable and the quantity insufficient. Yue had obeyed the stop, which mattered to safety. It did not make the lost balance a secret success or restore the usable inventory she no longer held.

reservoir_ep09_006.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_006.text: The room felt intolerably ordinary after the result. The tea complaint continued outside, and Deng's stool creaked when he moved. Yue had expected failure to announce itself with pain or a dramatic collapse. Instead she sat with a safe shoulder, a stopped circuit and a number whose plainness offered nowhere to hide. Mei asked her to describe the moment attention narrowed. Yue said she had wanted the trace to remain respectable. Speaking that desire made it smaller than the reservoir, though it had briefly governed the way she watched it.

reservoir_ep09_007.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_007.text: Deng helped her stand only after the familiar release had settled. She needed no lifting and accepted no unfamiliar shoulder movement. The ordinary clinician's next-day appointment remained booked for One Thousand One Hundred One, paid from the post-failure recovery line. Today's stop had found no immediate injury signs, but that observation did not replace tomorrow's review. Yue walked to the kitchen by the dry path. At its door she almost turned away because she did not want to answer a friendly question. Hunger brought her inside before pride could make the afternoon worse.

reservoir_ep09_008.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_008.text: Tian saw her bowl and asked whether he should discuss the river onion instead of the examination. Yue said the onion had passed every criterion required for a badly drawn onion. He took that as permission to describe its likely appetite. She ate while he invented a preference for burnt bread. After several spoonfuls she told him the warm condition had failed. He listened without arguing that she must secretly have passed. The joke remained available beside the disappointment, and she found she could hold both without falsifying either.

reservoir_ep09_009.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_009.text: Fu arrived from her ordinary shift and asked whether Yue wanted company on the short walk back. Yue accepted. Fu had heard nothing about the measured result until Yue chose to tell her. Their household calendar work had not purchased a right to her private candidate record. Yue explained the usable loss in plain terms, then admitted that she was angry at an ordinary warm room. Fu said she had once blamed a harmless bean for a quarrel with her brother. That confession helped more than advice about overcoming anger would have.

reservoir_ep09_010.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_010.text: At the room door Fu paused to ask whether they should postpone their next ordinary meal together. Yue checked the recovery plan and kept the modest invitation after its actual review. She did not need to turn every future pleasure into a reward contingent on passing. The paper fish beneath her window had tilted in the draft. She straightened it, then left its crooked tail alone. Her current reserve was smaller, her stage unchanged, and the evening still contained a bed she could use without proving she deserved it.

reservoir_ep09_011.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_011.text: On Day One Thousand One Hundred One, the ordinary clinician examined the actual post-temperature condition. Yue reported no new shoulder pain, no persistent headache and the attention narrowing recorded at the stop. The clinician checked her ordinary movement and tissue condition within the established range. No new injury was found. She was told to keep the next days reduced and perform no extra demand to chase the lost quantity. The appointment actually cost four coppers from the sixteen reserved for post-failure clinical checks, leaving twelve in that line.

reservoir_ep09_012.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_012.text: The clinician permitted the registered movement assessment on One Thousand One Hundred Four only if Yue remained recovered within its ordinary starting checks. Permission to assess was not a prediction of a pass. Deng adjusted the intervening lessons to short grounded releases, with no greater draw than the old practice already allowed. Yue resented the smallness for an hour. Then she noticed that the resentment itself kept urging her to add another sequence. She stopped after the scheduled lesson and went to mend the loose corner of her pillow cover.

reservoir_ep09_013.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_013.text: Jing set aside the materials actually consumed by the temperature attempt. Their cost was four coppers under the planned qualification material ceiling. The separate recovery replacement reserve would replace the used preparation for a later recovered trial after its actual issue, not erase today's consumption. Yue asked to see the stopped trace once more. Jing showed her its uneven change without enlarging it into a catastrophe. The preserved record was evidence of a specific failed response. It had no need to become a permanent description of Yue's courage.

reservoir_ep09_014.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_014.text: The pump-village candidate visited that afternoon with his latest cat letter. He had failed a different bounded condition and was angry at the phrase 'useful evidence.' Yue admitted that she disliked it too. They sat outside the kitchen and discussed what useful evidence actually felt like when it prevented the certificate they wanted. After a while he said he would rather know before returning to the well. She agreed, though agreement did not make either of them cheerful. The cat had stolen another fish and remained entirely indifferent to their conclusions.

reservoir_ep09_015.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_015.text: Day One Thousand One Hundred Two passed in reduced practice and ordinary rest. Yue took a short public walk, returned before she felt tired, and did not offer herself for a missed worker's shift. The course wage schedule had no accepted duty for her that day. A porter handled the bowls without her. She saw how easily the basin continued while she did less. The sight wounded one part of her pride and relieved another. Being needed for every small task would have made a paid recovery plan impossible to carry out.

reservoir_ep09_016.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_016.text: Deng asked her to notice the difference between a recovered body and an unchallenged one. She could feel comfortable while sitting and still meet difficulty under a changed condition. He kept the safe intake sets finite and recorded their actual input ceiling. Any later usable quantity would have to survive ordinary losses and independent sampling before they counted it. Yue completed the agreed modest sets, released and stopped. She did not turn their recorded gross input into a private number she could announce before Jing measured the current reserve.

reservoir_ep09_017.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_017.text: On Day One Thousand One Hundred Three, Jing prepared the ordinary movement route without Yue's qi. A low marker stood beside a dry, level turn. The permitted load would remain at waist height within its familiar weight and range. The route changed ordinary movement, not shoulder elevation, speed or load. Yue walked it once empty-handed under the clinician's retained limits. Her feet found the wider turn they had practiced. Mei wanted to observe whether the reservoir stayed balanced through that actual change, which no remembered seated result could answer.

reservoir_ep09_018.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_018.text: Tian offered to paint a fish on the movement marker. Jing refused because its edge was already visible and did not need decorative confusion. Tian accepted the refusal after a brief theatrical sigh. He painted the fish on his own scrap instead and gave it to the kitchen porter. Yue watched him choose another real place for the joke. An unaccepted addition had not destroyed his affection for the room. She wished she could move her own hopes as readily when a measured condition refused their first preferred location.

reservoir_ep09_019.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_019.text: The next morning's starting checks found Yue recovered for the bounded movement assessment. The ordinary room conditions were recorded, and the accepted blank settled. Jing measured seventy and a quarter usable after sleep and morning activity before the quarter-unit sample. Seventy remained after sampling. The compatible portion began at ninety-one and three quarters percent. Yue named the actual quantity without rounding it to the threshold. Her task would assess balance through a low ordinary turn, with the same familiar half-unit four-breath application and its existing output ceiling.

reservoir_ep09_020.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_020.text: The familiar application consumed half a unit, leaving sixty-nine and a half before the changed movement. Yue held the permitted light load close to her waist and walked the dry turn at ordinary speed. At the marked change she noticed the reservoir's response lag behind her intended release. She slowed rather than drawing harder. Mei gave the stop when the trace failed its balanced comparison. Yue grounded fully and handed the ordinary load to the appointed receiver. Nothing fell, and the safe handover did not make the balance acceptable.

reservoir_ep09_021.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_021.text: Jing measured sixty-eight and three quarters actually usable after the observed three-quarter-unit movement drift. Compatibility had fallen to ninety and three quarters percent. The movement condition had failed, independently of the earlier temperature result. Its start, sample, actual task and drift were recorded in that order. Yue had remained within the shoulder range and stopped without injury, yet the reservoir had not retained its registered balance through an ordinary turn. Mei signed the failed response. No helpful witness could substitute a more flattering account of what the trace had done.

reservoir_ep09_022.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_022.text: Yue asked whether her wider turn had been pointless. Deng said it had protected ordinary mechanics and kept the load safely controlled; those were real effects. It had not yet solved the reservoir's lag. She found herself wanting one correction to pay for every requirement. Deng shook his head before she could make the wish into an accusation. A room could need a better door latch and a better roof at the same time. Fixing the latch mattered, even on the rainy day when the roof still leaked.

reservoir_ep09_023.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_023.text: She took that image to the kitchen and found the porter complaining about an actual leaking roof corner. The coincidence irritated her until the porter asked for a dry cloth within her easy reach. She passed it to him and left the higher placement to another worker. The kitchen's repair arrangement belonged to its own budget and qualified ordinary work. Yue ate beneath the sound corner. Her meal did not improve the reservoir's lag, but her body needed food before tomorrow's review. She could do that necessary thing without making it heroic.

reservoir_ep09_024.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_024.text: On Day One Thousand One Hundred Five, the second actual post-failure clinical check found no new tissue injury from the movement assessment. Yue reported the lag, her slowed turn and the stopped application. The clinician checked the shoulder's established ordinary range and found it unchanged. Four more coppers paid this actual appointment, leaving eight in the post-failure clinical line. The changed-sleep assessment could remain provisionally scheduled for One Thousand One Hundred Eight if the intervening recovery and that morning's starting checks permitted its bounded demand.

reservoir_ep09_025.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_025.text: Deng kept the next practice smaller than Yue wanted. They worked on recognizing the stop before a low ordinary turn, with no test load and no claim of a passed movement condition. She could practice the recognition without rehearsing a qualifying result into existence. At one pause she spoke too early, then laughed at herself. Deng recorded the safe early stop and asked her to repeat after ordinary rest. The lesson ended on time. He had other candidates whose paid instruction did not disappear because Yue's disappointment felt urgent.

reservoir_ep09_026.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_026.text: That afternoon Zhou passed the courtyard and asked whether she wanted to discuss the measure room. Yue declined a new task but welcomed news. The corrected swollen measure had returned from ordinary repair and passed its receiving check. The customer's daughter had brought an apple for the workers who corrected the bill. Zhou had cut it among the actual shift. Yue had missed the apple, and he did not invent a saved piece. She liked that he told her anyway. The useful work remained useful after its small reward had been eaten.

reservoir_ep09_027.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_027.text: Fu joined Yue for the modest meal they had retained after the first review. They ate beans and ordinary bread at a low table. Fu described a disagreement over which household should borrow the garden's spare hoe next week. It required the actual owner's decision, which she had already requested. Yue listened without offering qi, authority or a new schedule. Her failed movement condition had made her wary of promising usefulness too quickly. Fu said listening was the thing she had wanted tonight, and continued the story until its absurd borrowed-hat detail made them laugh.

reservoir_ep09_028.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_028.text: On Day One Thousand One Hundred Six, Yue finished the private letter's description of the two stopped assessments. She did not dispatch it yet because the road information remained pending, but she refused to remove the failed results from the draft. Her mother knew what an ordinary shoulder limit cost. Yue wanted the letter to contain the real course, including its funded care, instead of another daughter-shaped promise that every difficult condition would soon be solved. She left the startled river onion beneath the account so the page could breathe.

reservoir_ep09_029.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_029.text: The registered changed-sleep condition used one ordinary interruption during the agreed night, with its duration and recovery recorded. It did not require a vigil or dangerous exhaustion. On Day One Thousand One Hundred Seven, Mei explained the arrangement again and checked that Yue could withdraw if her actual condition became unsuitable. Yue accepted after reading the stop criteria. The ordinary attendant would wake her at the agreed interval; afterward she could return to bed. No one had paid for a heroic struggle against sleep, and no such struggle would improve the examination.

reservoir_ep09_030.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_030.text: Before that night Yue folded her clothes where she could find them without reaching high. She ate the ordinary supper and went to bed at the registered time. At the agreed interruption the attendant knocked, confirmed her waking and recorded its actual duration. Yue returned to bed after the bounded ordinary task. Sleep came more slowly than she expected. She lay listening to the quiet corridor without drawing input, then finally rested again. In the morning she reported the delayed return honestly. The changed condition had happened to the body she brought to the table.

reservoir_ep09_031.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_031.text: On Day One Thousand One Hundred Eight, the starting review found Yue tired but recovered enough for the registered short stopped assessment. Her shoulder remained within its old condition, and she reported no headache before beginning. Mei reduced no criterion to make the tiredness convenient. Jing prepared the accepted blank and measured the present usable starting reserve at sixty-eight and a quarter after the actual interrupted night and morning activity. The lost night did not owe her yesterday's inventory. The quarter-unit sample left sixty-eight usable.

reservoir_ep09_032.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_032.text: The compatible portion began at ninety and a half percent. Yue saw how much of her response had already changed before the familiar task began. This result could not qualify under the preregistered standards. Mei asked whether Yue understood that the remaining bounded task would observe release under the changed night, not chase a pass. Yue answered yes and repeated the actual stop signal. Deng stood beside the low marker. The ordinary room was quiet, but she could hear her own wish to finish something impressive before everyone sent her to rest.

reservoir_ep09_033.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_033.text: She began within the old ceiling and lost the planned pause after the second ordinary breath. Mei gave the agreed stop immediately. Yue had consumed a quarter unit rather than the full half-unit task; the four-breath application was incomplete and could claim no finished quarter-unit useful output. She released before another draw. Jing's trace showed an additional half-unit drift during the interrupted response, leaving sixty-seven and a quarter actually usable. Compatibility had fallen to eighty-eight and three quarters percent. The changed-sleep assessment failed, with a stopped partial task recorded.

reservoir_ep09_034.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_034.text: A mild headache appeared after the stop. Yue named it instead of waiting to see whether she could hide it until the room emptied. The ordinary clinician's attendant checked her immediate condition, and the booked next-day review remained in place. There was no collapse and no restored reserve. She rested on the low seat until the headache eased enough for an ordinary accompanied walk. Deng carried his stool away himself. The unfinished task would remain unfinished; nobody proposed another breath to improve the appearance of the record.

reservoir_ep09_035.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_035.text: Mei compared the three stopped assessments without combining their best fragments. The warm response had drifted, the ordinary movement response had lagged, and changed sleep had broken the planned pause before completion. Three safe stops had prevented escalation. None supplied the three balanced, independently recovered qualifying trials the local certificate required. Yue remained stage seven. The measured quantity and compatible portion on this last morning were smaller than she had wanted to report, and the actual reduced reserve would govern what practice could safely follow.

reservoir_ep09_036.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_036.text: Jing put away the three sets of consumed assessment materials. Each stopped attempt had used four coppers of planned material, twelve in total. Their replacement for a later recovered series was funded by the separate twelve-copper recovery replacement line, but replacement would require actual accepted issue. New sleeves could not undo the samples or restore the qi drift. Yue watched the clean instrument return to custody. The room had done its job without becoming an enemy, and her failure did not give her ownership of anything on its shelves.

reservoir_ep09_037.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_037.text: Fu accompanied the ordinary walk after the headache had eased. Yue wanted to describe the partial task as nearly complete, then stopped herself. It had ended after two breaths, which was half of the familiar sequence and short of its rated completed output. Fu said she understood why the distinction hurt. A half-finished grain shift could contain hard work without earning the wage for a full accepted day. Yue disliked comparing herself to a shift and knew the comparison was accurate enough to keep. They walked at her ordinary comfortable pace.

reservoir_ep09_038.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_038.text: The kitchen gave Yue the meal already covered by the course's daily arrangement. The cook had saved no miraculous broth, only kept a covered bowl warm because the attendant reported a late arrival. Yue ate without trying to increase intake between mouthfuls. Her headache had eased but not entirely disappeared. Tian visited briefly, saw her tired face and left the paper fish conversation for another day. He asked whether she wanted the curtain lowered against the glare. She said yes, and he lowered it before returning to his actual shift.

reservoir_ep09_039.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_039.text: Rest was less satisfying than Yue had imagined when she was busy. The room contained no opponent to defeat and no applause for lying still. She heard workers outside moving the ordinary day forward while she remained under the course blanket. The paper fish shifted in the window draft. She watched until its repetitive motion became annoying, then turned it flat. That small choice changed the room without asking her body to prove anything. After a while she slept, and the sleep belonged to recovery rather than a hidden extra lesson.

reservoir_ep09_040.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_040.text: When she woke, the headache was duller. The attendant recorded that change and reminded her to report any return before the next-day appointment. Yue wanted to thank the attendant for being calm, but the woman had another patient to visit. She accepted the brief thanks and left. Yue noticed the habit of wanting helpful people to remain long enough to complete her feelings. Their actual work had an end beyond her room. She could be grateful without acquiring the rest of the attendant's afternoon.

reservoir_ep09_041.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_041.text: At dusk Deng visited only long enough to confirm tomorrow's ordinary review and the protected recovery plan. He did not set homework. Yue asked whether doing nothing would make the small circuit worse. He said they had stopped unnecessary demand, not erased the earned practice. Present rest could preserve the body in which that practice existed. She had wanted a more active answer and accepted this one reluctantly. Deng left before she could turn the visit into another supervised lesson. His stool remained in the practice pavilion where it belonged.

reservoir_ep09_042.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_042.text: The candidate who disliked squash sent a note with a drawing of an extremely offended turnip. It demanded an apology from the kitchen. Yue laughed softly and felt the headache remind her to stop laughing so hard. The note did not tell her that she had secretly succeeded. She preferred it for that reason. She placed the turnip beside the river onion and imagined a vegetable council too busy arguing to examine anybody. Then she ate the ordinary evening meal and returned to bed before the courtyard singers reached their disputed final verse.

reservoir_ep09_043.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_043.text: On Day One Thousand One Hundred Nine, the third paid post-failure clinical appointment examined the actual changed-sleep aftermath. Yue reported the partial task, measured drift, headache and its easing through ordinary rest. The clinician found no new tissue injury and no change to the shoulder's established limitations. The headache had resolved by the review, but the failed attention and balance still required reduced demand. Four coppers paid the actual appointment, leaving four of the original sixteen for the later recovery review. No unused appointment was presented as money already earned by Yue.

reservoir_ep09_044.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_044.text: The clinician prescribed eight protected rest days beginning One Thousand One Hundred Ten, followed by gradual already-earned practice and the fourth ordinary post-failure review on One Thousand One Hundred Twenty-five. The allocated twenty-four coppers paid three per actual protected day, supporting the agreed release from ordinary demands. It was not a wage for performing a concealed extra lesson. Yue read the dates and felt the possible family visit move farther into the future. The road windows had not changed, but the safely usable time before them had become smaller.

reservoir_ep09_045.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_045.text: Mei signed the failed assessment record before leaving for her other independent appointments. Yue asked if she regretted accepting the candidate place. Mei said the examination had been paid to discover the actual response. Regret was not a substitute for its result. She pointed to the three safe stops, which had preserved the possibility of future recovered work without certifying it today. Yue could choose whether to continue after recovery. Continuing would mean addressing the failures rather than requesting a warmer description of the same traces.

reservoir_ep09_046.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_046.text: Qiu came to arrange the actual protected interval with the course household and ordinary work receiver. There were no accepted wage duties scheduled inside the eight rest days. The two later possible ordinary work dates would be assessed after recovery, not silently reassigned today. Meals and the reserved bed continued through their own finite line. The protected recovery allowance came from the separate course reserve. Yue felt embarrassed that several people had to adjust around her stopped tasks. Qiu said the adjustment had been planned before they knew whether she would need it.

reservoir_ep09_047.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_047.text: Yue asked whether a protected day meant she could not visit the footbridge. The clinician's ordinary instructions permitted short comfortable movement within her present condition, while forbidding practice demand and tiring errands. Qiu told her to choose the short walk because she wanted its ordinary air, not because somebody might admire her prompt recovery. Yue recognized the second motive instantly. She had pictured walking to the bridge with a face that announced resilience. Instead she stayed for tea with Qiu and let the desire become less impressive before deciding.

reservoir_ep09_048.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_048.text: They drank the tea at the low table near the receiving desk. Qiu had been up before dawn for a household dispute and looked tired herself. Yue asked whether she wanted quiet. Qiu said she wanted somebody to complain to about the gate's new squeak. The repair was booked, and complaining would accomplish nothing beyond companionship. Yue welcomed that honest purpose. They discussed the squeak with unnecessary seriousness until Jing arrived and demonstrated a noise so inaccurate that both women began laughing. Yue stopped before the laughter became tiring.

reservoir_ep09_049.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_049.text: Jing later showed Yue the accepted order replacing the twelve coppers of assessment preparation consumed by the failures. The recovery replacement line was now fully committed for its stated materials, not available for a family fare. Jing would receive and check the actual stock before any later trial used it. The planned qualification material ceiling still had its own remaining forty after the original twelve had been consumed. Yue liked knowing that the replacement had a real source, then asked Jing to put the order away. She needed an afternoon containing something else.

reservoir_ep09_050.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_050.text: Jing brought out a worn cloth with a half-finished embroidered bean vine. Her father had declared the leaves inaccurate. Yue said she would consult him before planting an embroidered garden. They worked briefly at the low table, each stopping within ordinary comfort. Jing's stitches were neat; Yue's leaned toward one another as if whispering. She made only a small section and left it incomplete. The allowed ordinary handwork did not become disguised cultivation practice. Its unfinished vine could wait beside the failed examination without demanding that every incomplete thing share one meaning.

reservoir_ep09_051.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_051.text: Tian visited after his shift with an apple he had bought from his own actual wages. He divided it into four and asked whether Jing wanted a piece. Yue accepted one quarter. This was not the missed customer's apple restored by coincidence; Tian had seen a seller by the gate and wanted to bring something ordinary. He complained that the apple's skin was tougher than its middle. Jing said his knife needed ordinary sharpening. He agreed and borrowed the proper kitchen stone only after the cook accepted its return time.

reservoir_ep09_052.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_052.text: Watching Tian sharpen the knife under the cook's ordinary supervision, Yue thought about how often a difficult story could be improved by naming its small physical cause. The apple had not become hostile. The knife was dull. Her changed-condition failures had their own observed causes, more complicated than a dull edge but no more entitled to mystical excuses. She would need recovered work to change them. For tonight she could watch a friend complete an ordinary correction and eat the remaining apple piece before it browned.

reservoir_ep09_053.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_053.text: Fu arrived with a folded household invitation for a later garden meal, after the protected interval. She had left the date open for Yue's actual recovery rather than declaring it compulsory encouragement. Her brother had learned a new song and wanted an audience before anyone corrected its words. Yue said she was willing to be a skeptical listener. Fu wrote that phrase on the fold and promised to show him. Their friendship had room for a later visit whose timing respected a body neither of them could cure by being pleased to see the other.

reservoir_ep09_054.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_054.text: That evening Yue returned to the family letter. She added the third stopped assessment, the resolved headache and the eight actual protected days about to begin. She described the funded clinician and the fact that her earned small circuit remained intact while its harder reservoir conditions had failed. Then she wrote about the apple, the turnip and Jing's embroidered beans. The letter's center of gravity changed as she filled it. Her mother would receive news from a daughter living among people, rather than only a candidate awaiting permission to become worth hearing.

reservoir_ep09_055.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_055.text: She left the family road question for the later confirmed timetable. Wanting to visit did not mean the carrier could be booked from an unreported departure. The two work dates she might complete after recovery were still conditional on actual safe return. Yue marked that condition plainly in her private page. She had enough received money to support ordinary choices now; a longer family journey would wait until the reserved sum had an actual source. The old bargain had already taken years. She would not answer its loss with another promise made from unavailable time.

reservoir_ep09_056.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_056.text: Before bed Yue asked the attendant whether lowering the window curtain again was troublesome. The woman said the cord existed for exactly that purpose and demonstrated its low ordinary reach. Yue had looked at it all week without noticing that she could adjust it safely herself. She lowered the curtain and thanked the attendant for showing her. The room became softer around the lamp. Learning one small practical use did not raise a stage, but it returned a little agency during a week in which she had mostly been told to stop.

reservoir_ep09_057.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_057.text: She slept that night without a registered interruption. The sleep was ordinary recovery, not a passed changed-sleep trial. In the morning she would have no practice mat to attend, no independent sample to improve and no wage shift to rescue from another worker. The eight protected days would actually begin. Yue could feel the resistance gathering before the first one arrived. She named it silently, as Deng had taught her to name the urge before a delayed release. Naming did not remove it. It gave her a place from which to choose the next ordinary action.

reservoir_ep09_058.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_058.text: The paper fish rested flat beneath the window. Yue almost stood to set its tail in motion again, then decided it could remain still until morning. Outside, the gate squeaked and somebody complained with Qiu's exact degree of irritation. The sound made Yue smile rather than begin another sequence. She had failed three actual conditions under three different mornings. Those facts would remain in the record while her body rested. She extinguished the lamp and let the familiar earned circuit settle without asking it to make the record prettier.

reservoir_ep09_059.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_059.text: At first light the kitchen porter brought the ordinary breakfast to the protected room. Yue sat at the low table and ate while listening to workers begin the day outside. She wanted to join them and also wanted the headache never to return. Neither wish supplied the next safe practice date. The paid recovery arrangement had been made before her failure and now required its actual time. She put the empty bowl where the porter could retrieve it, opened the curtain by its low cord, and began the first day slowly.

reservoir_ep09_060.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_060.text: Beyond the window, water moved across the basin without waiting for her next number. The empty sky above it had no examination to pass. Yue watched the surface change under a light wind and felt both small and present. The reservoir inside her had lost usable quantity through real samples, work and drift. It would need actual recovered practice before another test. For the moment she had breakfast, a protected bed, ordinary company when wanted, and eight days whose purpose was to let the body carrying every future choice recover.

reservoir_ep09_061.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_061.text: Near the gate, a child cried because his paper boat had lodged beneath the bridge. Yue heard the cry and rose before remembering the protected interval. The child was not in danger; an adult had already taken a stick from the path shelf. Yue sat again and watched the boat come free under that adult's reach. The child cheered the stick. Her absence had harmed nobody. She let the lesson remain small instead of rewarding herself with a speech about how much wisdom she had gained.

reservoir_ep09_062.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_062.text: Jing knocked later with no instrument in her hands. She wanted to know whether Yue preferred quiet or a short account of her father's bean argument. Yue chose the beans. Apparently he had accused a neighboring gardener of flattering the soil instead of feeding it. Jing disagreed with both the accusation and its confidence. The visit lasted only a few minutes. When she left, Yue did not ask her to stay until loneliness disappeared. Company could be useful within a finite interval.

reservoir_ep09_063.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_063.text: The first protected payment was recorded for its actual day from the twenty-four-copper rest line. It supported the agreed release from ordinary demand, separate from the bed and meals already reserved. Yue did not spend it on extra materials or secretly hire an instructor for the afternoon. The money's purpose was time she could safely use without working to replace it immediately. Its size made the protection feel concrete. A lost day had not been declared priceless; somebody had reserved the means to let it pass.

reservoir_ep09_064.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_064.text: In the afternoon she reread her mother's plum-tree joke and remembered the first time they had argued about pruning. Yue had wanted every branch useful; her mother had preferred one low branch because its shadow reached the summer chair. That ordinary preference had survived years of harder costs. Yue could not return those lost years by becoming more cultivated. She could still ask about the chair, visit when the road and her body allowed, and listen to the answer without deciding beforehand what a successful daughter ought to hear.

reservoir_ep09_065.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep09_065.text: As the first protected evening approached, Yue found that she had accomplished almost nothing she could list as progress. The body felt calmer, the headache remained absent and she had obeyed the reduced interval. Those were actual observations, though they looked small beside her earlier imagined certificate. She ate the ordinary supper, left the failed traces with their proper custodian and kept the family letter private. Tomorrow would still require rest. She lay down before the courtyard grew loud and chose to let another unheroic night do its necessary work.
